💡 What makes a logo work here
  • Square, 512 × 512 px. The app icon on a phone home screen is square — a wide logo gets letterboxed with empty space either side.
  • PNG with a transparent background. Your titlebar takes the colour you pick below, so a logo baked onto a white square will show as a white block sitting on it.
  • One simple mark, not your full signage. It renders at 28 pixels in the titlebar — about the size of this text. A shop name in thin lettering turns to mush at that size.
  • Strong contrast against your titlebar colour. A dark logo on a dark navy bar disappears.
  • No logo? Leave it empty. The emoji beside this field, or your initials, reads far more clearly at small sizes than a squashed photo does.
Anything you upload is resized to 512 px automatically, so a photo straight off your phone is fine — it just will not look as sharp as a proper logo file.
The whole interface scales, not just the type, so nothing gets clipped. Staff can change it any time from the title bar.
🧾BIR / Tax setup (printed on every receipt)
Leave these blank if you are not yet BIR-registered — the POS still works. Fill them in once you have your Permit to Use so every receipt, X-Read and Z-Read carries the right identifiers.
Non-VAT stores print no VAT breakdown at all.
How long a customer may return an item. 0 = no limit.
👥Step 3 — Staff Accounts (PIN Login)
MyStore POS uses PIN-based login. Each staff member gets a 4-digit PIN. Up to 6 users. Role can be Manager or Cashier.
NameRolePIN (4 digits)

🔑 Defaults shown above are examples only — change them before you deploy.

⚠ About PIN security. PINs are hashed before they are written into the generated file, so they are not readable in the page source. But a 4-digit PIN is only 10,000 combinations, and if you publish to GitHub Pages the repository is public — treat these PINs as a till lock, not a vault. Give every staff member a different PIN, change them on a schedule, and never reuse a PIN you use anywhere else.

Pre-load your products. Leave empty to add everything inside the app.

NamePrice (₱)Cost (₱)StockBarcodeCategoryExpiryVAT-Ex

💡 Use stock 99 for services. Tick VAT-Ex for medicine and unprocessed food. CSV columns: name, price, cost, stock, barcode, category, vat_exempt, expiry — expiry as YYYY-MM-DD, blank for non-perishables

⚙Step 5 — Generate & Deploy

Everything is set. Generate your MyStore POS — download as a standalone HTML file, or package it as a GitHub Pages PWA (installable app).

🏢How many tills?
Multi-terminal — two or more tills sharing one stock count
Leave this off for a single till. The build stays completely offline: no server, no internet, no monthly cost, and no sync code in the file at all.
Turn it on only when two counters sell from the same stock. That needs a free Supabase project, and each till still keeps its own OR series and its own Z-Reading — which is what BIR requires anyway.
☁ Supabase setup — do these in order
  1. Create a free project at supabase.com. Any region near you; Singapore is closest to PH.
  2. Download the SQL below, open SQL Editor in Supabase, paste the whole file and press Run. It is safe to run more than once.
  3. Go to Authentication → Users → Add user and create one login per till (e.g. till1@yourstore.local, till2@yourstore.local) with a long random password each. Write the passwords down.
  4. Back in SQL Editor, run the three INSERT statements at the bottom of the SQL file. The first one returns your Store ID — copy that uuid.
  5. Open Project Settings → API and copy the Project URL and the anon / publishable key. The anon key is meant to be public; the SQL locks every table behind row-level security so only your till logins can read or write.
  6. Fill the four boxes below, set Terminal ID to TILL-01, and generate. Then change it to TILL-02 and generate again — one build per till.
  7. At each till: Settings → Multi-terminal sync, type that terminal’s password, press Save. The password is never put inside the file.
  8. On one till only, press Push this catalogue. Running it on both would count your stock twice.
Deliberately not collected here. A password baked into a published file is a password everyone has.
⚠ BIR. Two terminals are two machines. Each needs its own Permit to Use, MIN and serial, and files its own Z-Reading. Set those separately in Step 2 for each build. The SQL includes a daily_by_terminal view for combining the figures afterwards.
🔄Rebuild behaviour
Replace the product list on devices that already ran an older build
Leave this off for a live store — the till keeps its own stock counts, which are almost certainly more accurate than the ones in this form. Turn it on when you have genuinely revised the catalogue and want every device to take the new one. Sales history, customers and Z-readings are never touched.

📄 Step B — sw.js (Service Worker)

ⓘ This is a plain-text file. You will create it manually inside your GitHub repo — instructions below.

🚀 How to Deploy to GitHub Pages (Step by Step)
Step A — Upload the ZIP files
  1. Go to github.com → Sign in → click New repository
  2. Name it mystore-pos → set to Public → click Create repository
  3. Click "uploading an existing file" link on the empty repo page
  4. Extract the ZIP → drag all extracted files into the upload area (index.html, manifest.json, README.md, icon-192.png, icon-512.png)
  5. Scroll down → click Commit changes
Step B — Create sw.js manually
  1. In your repo, click Add file → Create new file
  2. Type exactly sw.js as the filename
  3. Copy the content from the sw.js box above (click Copy to Clipboard)
  4. Paste it into the file editor
  5. Click Commit changes → Commit directly to main → Commit changes
Step C — Enable GitHub Pages
  1. Go to your repo → click Settings tab
  2. Scroll down to Pages (left sidebar)
  3. Under Branch → select main → folder / (root) → click Save
  4. Wait about 1 minute → your POS is live at:
    https://username.github.io/repo/
📱 Install as App: Open the URL in Chrome (Android) or Safari (iPhone) → tap ⋮ menu → Add to Home Screen → opens fullscreen like a native app!
